nb9a1ff2c390d: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEP TA-Ce , with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEP TA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEP TA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.
nbd522bc8cdd3: Clay minerals are the most crucial constituents in brickmaking clays, yet the specific role of different clay minerals remain poorly understood due to their natural coexistence and formidable challenges of separation. Here, we design a kaolinite-illite-quartz-feldspar system through a multiple-stage purification strategy, enabling direct evaluation of two of the most critical clay minerals for brick making - kaolinite and illite. Precise tuning the initial clay mineral assemblage yields brick strengths up to 8.5 times the ASTM C62 Grade MW requirement, without upgrading existing production methods. Mineralogical mechanisms responsible for substantial strength enhancement are revealed. Extensive analyses of 60 brick formulations uncovered a breakdown of conventional linear relationships among different brick properties due to the temperature-dependent responses of kaolinite and illite; specific formation pathways of mullite and amorphous phases; and over-firing defects above 1200 °C due to K + -induced fluxing from illite. Notably, a previously unrecognized negative correlation between mullite and brick strength is identified, suggesting a need to reconsider the widely held assumption of mullite as a strengthening phase. This work not only presents insights for optimizing high-strength brick formulations but also opens avenues for investigating the intricate contributions of distinct starting components to key brick performance.
n17be68ba099e: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.
n7ede072627bb: The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.
n112ffef7007f: Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.
n2d5c96e16337: Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. PDH is often dysregulated in metabolic diseases and cancer. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues. This mechanism enables cells to efficiently fight oxidative stress. Under oxidative stress, cells execute a metabolic shift, blocking glycolytic flux into the TCA cycle to shunt glycolytic carbons toward the pentose phosphate pathway. This generates NADPH which cells use to detoxify H 2 O 2 and to reduce oxidized cysteines. We find that DLAT oxidation is required for cells to mount an effective antioxidant response. Mutations preventing DLAT oxidation render PDH resistant to oxidative inhibition, impair NADPH generation, reduce peroxide detoxification, and sensitize cells to oxidative damage and death. DLAT oxidation also drives a Warburg-like metabolic phenotype of increased glucose uptake, elevated lactate secretion, and reduced TCA cycle activity. Thus DLAT oxidation is a redox-sensing mechanism that regulates PDH activity and central carbon metabolism.
nbe39d700d6ec: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. To resolve this problem, we hypothesize the existence of simpler HK97-fold viral capsids associated with smaller genomes than those of known HK97-fold viruses. Such small viral genomes are searched in environmental metagenomes across public databases, including IMG/M and MGnify. Using hidden Markov models and protein language models, we identify and characterize small viral genomes encoding HK97-fold proteins that exhibit molecular similarities to encapsulins yet lack portal and tail genes. The phylogenetic analyses of HK97-fold proteins reveal independent mixed groups of viruses and encapsulins, and structural analyses identify similarities between encapsulins and procapsids, the immature state of viral capsids. The observations support a bidirectional evolution between encapsulins and HK97-fold viruses enabled by the viral procapsid state. Using biophysical and genomic arguments, we introduce an evolutionary model of HK97-fold protein shells, predicting that they emerged as lower-symmetry biochemical compartments and that HK97-fold viral capsids may retain biochemical functions.
n534cc1bfc2ae: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200–400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr 0.8 Y 0.2 O 2.9 and BaZr 0.4 Ce 0.4 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 2.9 , as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO 3 -based phases (LSGM), and Bi 2 V 0.7 Sb 0.3 O 5.5 . Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO 2 -containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

n034f691828a2: Preterm birth is associated with breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance and remains the leading cause of global mortality in young children. However, the role of self-reactive antibodies has been limited to a handful of pathogenic allo- and autoantibodies linked to pregnancy complications. Here we identify a shared autoreactive signature of pregnancy in pregnant sera (n = 2,719) relative to never-pregnant controls (n = 130), using proteome-wide autoantibody profiling. Across eight human pregnancy cohorts, we define autoreactivities associated with preterm birth by comparing preterm (n = 688) and term (n = 1,505) pregnancies. Within the signature, antibodies to IL1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) induce resorption, inflammation and vascular malperfusion in pregnant mice. IL1RA localizes to placental endothelial adherens junctions, suggesting a role in vascular integrity. These findings identify a term pregnancy humoral immune program and shared changes preceding preterm delivery, including anti-IL1RA, which may have direct pathogenic consequences. nce49a071996a: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. na4ab586395a6: Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.
n103f79be046f: NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment.However, the effects of chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy regimens on NAD metabolism remain unclear. n40c0f0a679bb: Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and <1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.
nfcbfbfc20d09: Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst with a wide range of applications. Here, the authors demonstrate that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly active solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst.
nc841188a5ffa: Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.
nc488dfbfea08: Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.
nadcd4fd1363e: Traditional methods struggle to quantify the optical heterogeneity in nanomaterials. Here the authors develop a new spectroscopic tool that rapidly extracts trends in single-particle spectra and apply it to ZnSeTe nanocrystals, revealing the origin of their low color purity.
n49266935d90e: Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

n757c733fc5e6: Soils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0–90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. Abundant sialidases in deep soils implicate glycoproteins as a key carbon source. Warming effects are smaller and decrease over time but are depth-specific: surface soils show enhanced amino sugar and sugar alcohol transport, phosphorus mobilization, and stress tolerance, whereas mid- and deep soils exhibit stimulated C1 metabolism, CO oxidation, and altered nitrogen turnover. These depth-specific microbial trait shifts may critically influence soil carbon–climate feedbacks.

n0ac9fe5c24d1: Magnetic order in van der Waals magnets can strongly influence their lattice dynamics, yet how it affects local and macroscopic manifestations of spin-phonon coupling remains unclear. Optical phonons probe bond-scale exchange modulation and short-range spin correlations, whereas long-wavelength acoustic modes couple to uniform strain fields and are sensitive to renormalization of the macroscopic elastic tensor associated with long-range magnetic order. Experimentally accessing these acoustic excitations in low-dimensional crystals is challenging due to their low energies and the small lateral dimensions of exfoliated samples. Here, we employ Brillouin–Mandelstam scattering spectroscopy to investigate surface acoustic phonons in exfoliated NiPS 3 thin films across the antiferromagnetic transition. Our results show a single Rayleigh surface mode whose phase velocity decreases significantly across the Néel temperature. This anomaly reflects a strong magnetoelastic renormalization of the elastic constants triggered by the onset of antiferromagnetic order. First-principles calculations, combined with continuum finite-element modeling reproduce the Rayleigh-wave dispersion and its magnetic-order–induced shift. The results reveal how microscopic exchange interactions govern the macroscopic elastic response of two-dimensional antiferromagnetic semiconductors, enabling magnetically tunable phononic, magnonic, and strain-mediated spintronic devices.

nbcf7685a35c6: Accurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions. The model accurately reconstructs both network structure and mobility flows, yielding epidemic spreading trajectories that closely match those obtained using real mobility data. Furthermore, the method can be effectively implemented using open data on flight routes and airport traffic, reducing dependence on proprietary datasets. Our approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for scenario analysis and policy design in global mobility systems.
n3d470a7b5708: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are the guardians of translational fidelity. Their complex function is mirrored by an elaborate structure, which includes multiple nested domains. While the evolutionary pressures that promoted the emergence of some domains, such as the editing domain, are clear, the pressures acting on other domains, particularly those at the C-terminus, are not. Here, we combine kinetic analysis, X-ray crystallography, and bioinformatics to unveil the history and evolutionary forces that have shaped isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase (IleRS) domain structure. We find that the traditional classification of IleRSs based on the C-terminal tRNA-recognition domains is incomplete, as it fails to capture features of the synthetic domain. Guided by a crystal structure of the Priestia megaterium IleRS2:tRNA Ile complex, we removed key interactions between IleRS2 and its cognate tRNA and characterised their impact on enzyme activity. We found that D-loop interactions with the IleRS2 C-terminal domains are non-essential in prokaryotes, and their loss can even increase catalytic turnover. Further, we show that the zinc-binding domain of IleRS1 recognises the anticodon less stringently than the canonical C-terminal domain of IleRS2. Our data suggest that C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of IleRSs is an ongoing process with a historical precedent and is consistent with selection for faster aminoacylation rate.
nd6b8fcadd6b6: Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. However, their vulnerability to noise limits the accuracy of simulations. Here, we establish a continuous-time framework for mitigating noise in analogue quantum simulation. Our protocol fully preserves the continuous-time nature by avoiding any active control or measurement of the system during the dynamics, while achieving exact noise cancellation. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Furthermore, the protocol is Hamiltonian-independent and robust to realistic ancilla noise. This work points to a promising direction for achieving high-fidelity analogue quantum simulation in the presence of noise.
n65249c0242a8: Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

n01b97ded6e89: Cancer cachexia is a wasting syndrome with outsized impact on morbidity and mortality, yet its drivers and systemic consequences remain poorly defined. In this study, we repurposed longitudinal clinicogenomic data from 52,236 patients with cancer profiled by MSK-IMPACT (2010–2024) at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center to define episode-resolved trajectories of consensus-defined cachectic weight loss and linked these events to outcomes, serology and tumor genotypes. Cachectic episodes clustered near periods of disease progression and were associated with inferior outcomes in nearly all cancer types. Across diverse malignancies, cachectic weight loss episodes exhibited a consistent serologic signature characterized by lower albumin and hemoglobin and higher levels of liver enzymes. Numerous somatic tumor genotypes, including TP53 mutation across several diseases, were also associated with more frequent onset of cachectic episodes. Motivated by these observations, we developed a multivariate model to predict impending risk of cachectic weight loss in patients with lung, colorectal and prostate cancer, validated in an independent, external cohort from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (n = 5,785). Routine clinicogenomic data are, therefore, a scalable resource for discovery in cancer cachexia. Using longitudinal data from 52,236 patients with cancer, this study created a multimodal atlas of cancer cachexia, demonstrating that weight loss episodes are linked to systemic serologic signatures and specific tumor genotypes and can be predicted using integrated clinical and molecular data, enabling earlier identification.

n23b287ead930: Clinical prediction models are increasingly deployed to support diagnostic and prognostic decisions, making reproducibility essential for assessing their reliability and generalizability. Analytical code supports independent assessment of these processes, yet its availability in the literature remains limited. This scoping review quantifies current practices in sharing analytical code to inform the development of TRIPOD-Code, a reporting guideline for code availability and reproducibility. Here a large-language-model-assisted pipeline was developed to screen articles citing TRIPOD or TRIPOD+AI, extract repository links and assess retrieved repositories against 14 predefined reproducibility-related features. Among 3,967 articles, 482 (12.2%) included code-sharing statements. Sharing prevalence varied widely by journal and country. Repository assessment showed substantial heterogeneity in reproducibility features. These findings underscore the need for clearer expectations beyond code availability, including documentation, dependency specification and executable structure. Strengthening these practices may improve the usability of clinical prediction model studies and support their deployment in real-world clinical settings. An analysis of code availability in the open-access published literature shows that code sharing in clinical prediction models remains limited and reveals significant variability in practices and documentation quality.

n4dd3906d7305: Programmable quantum devices provide a platform for controlling the coherent dynamics of quantum wave functions. Monitoring and feedback can control classically chaotic dynamics, but extending these approaches to quantum systems is challenging because chaotic evolution amplifies perturbations and is sensitive to noise and decoherence. Here we demonstrate adaptive monitored quantum circuits that incorporate conditional feedback into non-unitary evolution, using local mid-circuit measurements and resets to control quantum chaotic dynamics. We perform the experiments on an IBM superconducting quantum processor with up to 100 qubits, implementing a quantum version of the classically chaotic Bernoulli map. The map scrambles quantum information, whereas local measurements and feedback attempt to steer the dynamics towards a fixed point of the map. This competition drives a dynamical phase transition between quantum and classical dynamics, which we observe experimentally and describe theoretically using noisy simulations, matrix product states and mappings to statistical mechanics models. By successfully applying up to nearly 5,000 entangling gates and 5,000 non-unitary mid-circuit operations on systems up to 100 qubits, the quantum processor yields accurate estimates of the universal critical properties. Controlling quantum chaos requires using measurement and feedback that survive noise and decoherence. Such control is now achieved in a superconducting quantum processor and reveals a critical transition between quantum and classical dynamics.

n8578cfe7cc73: The Sun continuously releases a stream of charged particles known as the solar wind, threaded by magnetic field lines that occasionally fold back on themselves in sharp reversals called magnetic switchbacks. These structures are frequently observed by spacecraft near the Sun, but their formation mechanism remains an open question. Using measurements from Solar Orbiter at 0.55 AU, we report heavy ion observations within a magnetic switchback that provide direct evidence of its solar source. Elevated charge-state ratios of oxygen and carbon, combined with a depletion of helium relative to protons, indicate that the switchback plasma originated from hot, closed coronal loop structures. A semi-empirical coronal model, constrained by electron temperature and density measurements from the Solar Dynamics Observatory, traces the ion signatures to either a coronal hole boundary or loops within the coronal hole, implicating the source mechanism as interchange reconnection, where closed loops reconnect with open magnetic field and eject plasma. The proton velocity and magnetic field fluctuations of the switchback are in accordance with an outward-propagating Alfvén wave. These findings suggest that interchange reconnection and wave or turbulence mechanisms jointly govern switchback origin and propagation, respectively. Most importantly, we show that switchbacks preserve measurable signatures, carrying information about the physical processes that heat the solar atmosphere and accelerate the solar wind.

n1fb12d5b6ff8: Many white dwarfs accrete the debris of disrupted planetary bodies, detected in the form of metal enrichment in their atmospheres, dusty or gaseous circumstellar discs, and photometric transits from debris. The composition of accreted debris has been shown to be diverse yet overall closely resembles Solar System bodies. Here we report the discovery of a white dwarf accreting material that is unlike any Solar System object. The atmosphere of HS 0209+0832 is strongly enriched in trans-iron elements including zinc, copper and niobium but depleted in the canonical rock-forming elements silicon and iron. The composition of the accreted object is consistent with a candidate second-generation planet, formed from the stellar material ejected during the giant phase. The key abundance signature that differentiates it from a first-generation planet is the high enrichment of s-process elements. Photospheric helium and the absence of terrestrial rock-forming elements implies that the white dwarf is accreting from the escaped atmosphere of a photo-evaporating giant planet candidate. This is further supported by the detection of a sinusoidal photometric period of 4.399 ± 0.026 days at an amplitude of 0.120% ± 0.018%, which we attribute to thermal emission phase variability from a planetary day–night cycle or a transiting cometary tail of an evaporating gas giant. The discovery of this second-generation planet that is chemically distinct from first-generation material demonstrates that close-in planets around white dwarfs can form after the main sequence.

n5d4e94b74903: The GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide preserves kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. Here we report a 52-week randomized trial of subcutaneous semaglutide 1 mg once weekly versus placebo (n = 106 (n = 25 women, n = 81 men)) in participants with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease. To identify kidney-specific mechanisms of action for semaglutide, we performed integrated multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging of the kidney and biopsy for histology (n = 33), alongside single-nucleus (n = 22) and spatial transcriptomics (n = 13) on paired samples with before- and after-treatment measurements. Coprimary magnetic resonance imaging outcomes (oxygenation by R2*, global perfusion and tissue inflammation by T1 mapping) were not significantly altered by semaglutide versus placebo treatment. Secondary outcomes revealed that semaglutide treatment, as compared to placebo, was associated with a significantly reduced renal artery resistive index and stabilization of the apparent diffusion coefficient, indicating prevention of fibrosis progression. Moreover, secondary transcriptomic outcomes revealed pronounced effects of semaglutide on glomerular endothelial cells, consistent with the results of spatial analyses indicating reduced numbers of immune cells in the proximity of these endothelial cells. The results from this trial indicate that mechanisms of kidney protection by semaglutide may include reduced vascular resistance, prevention of fibrosis and improved underlying molecular programs promoting endothelial cell health. n136ed7658c54: Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are standard of care for resectable stage IIIB–D melanoma, but knowledge gaps remain regarding optimal treatment type, long-term survival, postsurgical management and clinical, histopathological or molecular subgroups. nc74c55b8ddc8: Liquid chromatography is a predominant technology for the separation of small molecules. In the first step, a machine-learning model predicts a retention order index, taking into account chromatographic conditions. In the second step, we map predicted indices to absolute retention times. Our 2-step method outperforms existing methods that were trained on the target dataset. Finally, we systematically study what chromatographic conditions result in notable changes of retention order. A method for transferable retention time prediction across chromatographic conditions and compound classes is presented. The approach makes use of a two-step strategy that first predicts a condition-aware retention order index followed by mapping it to absolute retention times.
naa76afd8a6b6: There are no currently approved therapies that promote new myelin formation after myelin damage, which can, in part, be attributed to a lack of reliable systems that can reproducibly model these processes. n524dbae5bfc0: Aging and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) are accompanied by alterations to large-scale communication patterns in the brain, which can be tracked in vivo using functional connectivity. These findings together suggest that both AD and aging alter major but orthogonal functional pathways in the brain. More broadly, our findings position whole-brain connectivity dynamics as a unifying framework for interpreting functional changes across the adult lifespan.

n5acdbdbab64a: Below every step we take there is groundwater. Out-competing rivers, lakes and wetlands in terms of water quantity and quality, shallow aquifers are an essential reservoir of freshwater for the human population. At the same time, they represent the largest freshwater biome on earth, forming a responsive but vulnerable interface between the highly dynamic surface aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems and the environmentally static deeper zones of the subsurface. Shallow aquifers are home to a vast phylogenetic and functional microbial diversity, regularly surpassing those of surface environments. Predominantly colonized by microorganisms, key drivers of community composition and biogeochemical cycles are the hydrogeological settings, availability of energy and prevailing redox conditions, as well as climate and local to regional anthropogenic activities. Although there is steadily growing knowledge on microbial biodiversity and their potential functions, quantitative data on active key processes, such as carbon cycling, are scarce. We do have a very incomplete idea of the abundances and distribution of viruses, protists and fungi and their ecological role in groundwater. In this Review, we discuss current and future pressures to shallow groundwater ecosystems in terms of microbial community dynamics particularly in light of global and climate change, that is, groundwater pollution and warming. In this Review, Karwautz and Griebler examine the microbial communities found in shallow groundwater and aquifers, exploring their diversity, functional roles and dynamic interactions with adjacent terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, as well as the influence of global change and anthropogenic pressures on these microorganisms.
n4b9ffc1314b2: Microorganisms facilitate both the synthesis and breakdown of bio-based biodegradable plastics, which positions them as central players in the development of a future circular plastics economy. In this Review, we discuss the contributions of microorganisms across the life cycle of key bio-based polymers, focusing on polyhydroxyalkanoates, bacterial nanocellulose, and the monomers of polylactic acid and polyethylene furanoate, and we critically assess the extent to which current microbial capabilities can support polymer synthesis and degradation. Although the genetic capacity for these processes is widespread, this does not necessarily translate into efficient synthesis or biodegradation in industrial or environmental conditions. Microbial synthesis remains constrained by low volumetric productivity, carbon inefficiencies and downstream processing challenges, whereas biodegradation is highly dependent on material properties and environmental conditions, with efficient biodegradation often limited to managed settings. Thus, achieving an effective circular bio-based plastic economy requires the integration of microbial engineering, polymer chemistry, material science and other disciplines to optimize both production and end-of-life management. In this Review, O’Connor and colleagues discuss the contributions of microorganisms across the life cycle of key bio-based polymers and assess the current role, the potential and limitations of microbial production and degradation of bio-based polymers as well as the implications for integration of microbiological processes into a circular bioeconomy.

n4cd35d4072be: Zabilugene almadenorepvec (VCN-01) is a hyaluronidase-expressing oncolytic adenovirus with a favorable safety profile and encouraging antitumor activity in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. n84170acbdbde: Antibody-based single-cell technologies, such as flow cytometry, mass cytometry and CITE-seq, have become widely used in clinical diagnostics and basic research; however, their analysis is complicated by technical noise, batch effects, platform differences and restricted antibody panels. n8c44ab98ebee: Motivated by the successes of large language models (LLMs), we hypothesized that semantic information in the brain may be expressed in distributed patterns of neural activity. nb351735dbb2c: Understanding how neurons integrate into developing circuits and contribute to functional activity is essential for decoding brain development and plasticity. n59c3de900ae2: Entanglement in multiphoton graph states is an important resource for applications such as measurement-based quantum computing and memoryless quantum repeaters. However, most experimental demonstrations have only successfully prepared small-scale instances. A method known as fusion provides a divide-and-conquer approach that can link smaller resource states into larger, more complex graphs. Its practical scalability in linear optical systems has been limited by the probabilistic nature of conventional fusion protocols, which necessitates extensive hardware overhead and feed-forward resources to achieve deterministic outcomes. Here we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a deterministic fusion operation on a superconducting circuit device with built-in error mitigation. Our scheme can connect small time-bin-encoded cluster states that are generated on demand into larger, reconfigurable photonic graph states of increased size. We implement fusion by non-destructively projecting pairs of flying microwave photons into Bell states. The protocol involves the active reset and reuse of superconducting qubits to circumvent the effects of decoherence. We demonstrate genuine multipartite entanglement across 13 photonic qubits, establishing a scalable framework for photonic graph-state synthesis. Graph states entangle many photons in a special structure that is useful for several quantum protocols. Making graph states is often probabilistic and inefficient, but now a deterministic approach using superconducting qubits has been demonstrated.
n4105c730e16a: Non-equilibrium systems challenge the standard definitions of phases and phase transitions from equilibrium statistical physics. Here we show that the onset corresponds to an activity-driven phase transition, marked by the emergence of a system-spanning critical backbone of vorticity nodal lines. Below this threshold, vorticity structures are fragmented and vortex centres form only finite, mechanically floppy networks. Above this threshold, the nodal lines of the vorticity field percolate and the vortex centres form a rigid, system-spanning cluster. The geometric transition is characterized by the emergence of critical percolation statistics for the vorticity nodal lines, whereas the mechanical transition reflects the emergence of a vortex configuration that shows rigidity percolation statistics for vortex centres. We show that both transitions are absent in equilibrium systems that obey detailed balance, demonstrating that the transition is intrinsically non-equilibrium. These results establish an experimentally accessible definition of fully developed active turbulence, linking microscopic activity to macroscopic geometry, and mechanics of living systems. The continuous energy injection in active fluids leads to active turbulence. Now, geometric and mechanical analyses reveal a phase transition that leads to fully developed active turbulence.
n8d87ca187a78: The rational design of soft drugs has emerged as a powerful strategy to enhance drug safety, without compromising efficacy. Unlike conventional active pharmaceutical ingredients, soft drugs are deliberately designed to undergo predictable and rapid metabolic inactivation after exerting their therapeutic effect. Regarding topical administration, the soft drug approach enables potent local activity while minimizing systemic exposure and toxicity. However, despite these advantages and the market approval of several soft drugs, especially in dermatological, inhaled and gut-restricted therapies, the concept remains underutilized and often misunderstood, frequently being conflated with prodrugs. This Review revisits the concept of soft drugs from a modern perspective, clarifies its distinction from related approaches, highlights recent clinical successes in topical delivery, and provides practical insights into the application of soft drug design in drug discovery. Soft drugs are designed to enhance drug safety, undergoing rapid and predictable metabolic inactivation after exerting their therapeutic effect. This review provides an overview of the principles of soft drug design, highlighting examples of topical soft drugs in development, practical considerations, ongoing challenges and future directions.
n2679ce699ac6: Microbial interventions offer sustainable opportunities to enhance soil health and ecosystem functioning, but they can also have unintended ecological consequences. n1d8c0250ec13: The first generation of stars, known as population III (Pop III), formed from primordial gas consisting solely of hydrogen and helium and is believed to have emerged only a few hundred million years after the Big Bang. This less chemically evolved system may have provided favourable conditions for preserving the absorption signatures of Pop III enrichment. We infer a minimum dark matter halo mass of $$\mathrm{log}({M}_{{\rm{h}},\min }/{M}_{\odot })=10.6{8}_{-1.72}^{+0.93}$$ , supporting late-time Pop III formation at the outskirts of atomic hydrogen cooling haloes. Our findings open a promising observational pathway to identifying the chemical imprints of the first stars and constrain the conditions for their formation. The discovery of an unusually metal-poor galaxy overdensity that may preserve the chemical fingerprints of the first stars in the Universe provides a new way to investigate how the earliest stellar generations formed.
n0477b1626698: The mid-infrared spectrum of star-forming, high-metallicity galaxies is dominated by emission features from aromatic and aliphatic bonds in small carbonaceous dust grains, often referred to as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). n9d854931f2dc: Safiglipron is an oral small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist administered without fasting or dietary restrictions. n5e2ee2338dfe: Reproducibility has long been considered a foundation of trustworthy science, yet practices that enable reproducible research remain inconsistently implemented, despite widespread awareness and establishment of policies and guidelines. Biomedical research that cannot be reproduced can lead to resource waste and adversely impact patient safety, public health outcomes, scientific progress and public trust. Here we provide an overview of the current landscape of reproducible research in the biomedical sciences, summarize current efforts to harmonize terminology and implementation, and highlight the persistent barriers to adoption of best practices. We outline a practical framework to promote more uniform implementation and explore future directions for advancing reproducibility across stakeholders in the research process, including researchers, institutions, journals and funders. Reproducibility is a foundational principle of trustworthy science, but reproducible research practices are not consistently implemented. This Review summarizes the current landscape including efforts to harmonize terminology and implementation, persistent barriers and ecosystem responses.
nfa1c97e9a36c: Werner syndrome helicase (WRN) is a synthetic lethal target for microsatellite instability (MSI) cancers. n243dd020bb75: Mental imagery is a hallmark of human cognition, yet its neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. ne4e6592f02d9: The behavioral effects of anesthetics are highly conserved across species, hinting at shared and fundamental underlying mechanisms. This reveals a conserved dynamical profile of anesthesia across species, characterized by shorter intrinsic timescales of neural activity and dampened inter-regional synchrony. Deep-brain stimulation of the macaque centromedian thalamus reverses this profile and restores behavioral responsiveness. This conserved dynamical phenotype covaries with conserved transcriptional profiles of excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission. Biophysical modeling provides a potential mechanistic link between the macroscale dynamical phenotype of anesthesia and microscale effects of key molecular targets on the timescales of synaptic excitation and inhibition. These analyses reveal a shared neural endpoint of anesthesia: across species and scales, anesthetics induce spatiotemporal isolation of local neural activity.
nc792592103c6: General anesthetics seem to work in all living species. This raises the question of whether there are common changes in neural activity that occur during transitions between wakefulness and anesthesia. A landmark study by Luppi and colleagues now reveals a conserved dynamic signature of anesthesia that spans hundreds of millions of years of evolution.
nd00a15aa49fc: Complex fluids display unusual flow behaviour that originates from their microstructure, but observing this structure has been challenging. Now, X-ray scattering microscopy is fast enough to follow the tumbling of nanoparticles.
n4f3e06f28063: Complex fluids transition from laminar to transitional flow above a critical control parameter, in a similar manner to their Newtonian counterparts. In a continuum mechanics sense, fluid elements follow the ensuing complex trajectories, which gives rise to secondary flows in terms of macroscopic vortices. However, it is not known whether their trajectories exhibit the same spatiotemporal behaviour as the macroscopic flow field if idealized fluid elements are replaced with actual anisotropic nanoparticles. Here, to address this fundamental question, we develop a multiscale method that combines small-angle X-ray scatter microscopy with polarized light imaging, thereby bridging seven orders of magnitude in length scales. We demonstrate proof of principle for Taylor–Couette flow—a classical transitional flow problem—of platelet-like graphene oxide nanoparticle and rod-like cellulose nanocrystal suspensions. The analysis shows markedly different multiscale dynamics underlying flow stability: whereas the platelet-like particles follow the macroscopic dynamics of the secondary flows, as expected for high rotational Péclet numbers, the rod-like particles exhibit characteristic high-frequency orientational motion at moderate rotational Péclet numbers that correlates with the turnover frequency of the vortex instabilities. The trajectories of embedded particles provide a route for probing fluid flow dynamics. An X-ray scatter microscopy approach that enables precise monitoring of non-sphericalnanoparticles now reveals multiscale dynamics in complex fluids.
ned009d8eaf3f: Psychedelic protects against chemotherapy-induced nerve damage
nf2708f19f446: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate every step of cellular RNA metabolism, and their dysregulation contributes to many diseases. This Perspective describes the endogenous and disease-linked roles of RBPs and strategies for their therapeutic targeting, including opportunities that arise from the recent discovery of RBPs localized to the cell surface.
ndc06e0592b3e: In this Perspective, the authors use examples from evolution, animal models of disease and clinical results to explore how IFNγ, a quintessential antipathogen cytokine, also has a fundamental role in tissue homeostasis and organ function through its effects on non-haematopoietic structural cells.
n3853cab5b568: Modern observatories such as JWST and ALMA are revealing dynamically mature galaxies early in cosmic history. A century after Hubble, galaxy morphology is becoming a probe of galaxy-formation physics, including gas accretion, star formation and feedback.
n942aca57ab7e: New observations provide a more robust observational test of tidal torque theory while revealing an unexpected puzzle for galaxy formation.
n3074fcd0d0bc: AGENT, an AI-driven framework integrating high-throughput experimentation with Bayesian optimization, enables the rapid engineering of thermostable, solid-state mRNA vaccines. These formulations retained full bioactivity after storage at 37 °C for 2 months, elicited immune responses non-inferior to fresh vaccines, and enabled cold-chain-free delivery via microneedle patches in rodents and nonhuman primates.
n3d4e93bdcaf1: The instability of mRNA−lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) necessitates ultra-cold storage, limiting global distribution and their broader application in advanced delivery systems. Solid-state, water-free formulations enhance thermostability and enable integration into emerging delivery modalities such as microneedle patches. Previous efforts to stabilize mRNA−LNPs have been constrained by narrow formulation scope and low-throughput screening methods. Here we introduce Algorithm-Guided Experimental design for lipid Nanoparticle Thermostabilization (AGENT), an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework that couples high-throughput experimentation with Bayesian optimization to identify thermostable mRNA−LNP formulations. AGENT extracts maximal information from sparse experimental datasets, enabling efficient formulation optimization in six iterations completed within 1 month. We stabilized mRNA vaccines with two clinically relevant LNPs representative of the Moderna (SM-102-based) and Pfizer-BioNTech (ALC-0315-based) compositions into solid-state formulations that retained 100% bioactivity after storage at 37 °C for more than 2 months. In rodents and non-human primates, thermostable, solid-state vaccine formulations induced antigen-specific immune responses non-inferior to those elicited by intramuscular delivery of freshly prepared soluble vaccines. The thermostability of RNA vaccines is improved with AI.
ne2528e8dfdd3: Author Correction: Bioinstructive implantable scaffolds for rapid in vivo manufacture and release of CAR-T cells
n7951af0c969b: Lipid nanoparticles often show reduced performance when delivering the large messenger RNAs that encode gene editors. Screening ionizable lipids with a gene-editor-sized RNA identified LC-1, which forms a structure that enhances endosomal escape and enables efficient genome editing in the liver, lung and brain of mice.
n45e9fe345a80: Although lipid nanoparticles are clinically validated for RNA delivery, their potency often declines as transcript size increases. Here we report a large-cargo-informed lipid discovery strategy that incorporates mRNA size into ionizable lipid screening. A combinatorial library of 384 lipids was screened using a 5.7-kb ABE–NanoLuc reporter mRNA, identifying large-cargo-optimized lipids led by LC-1. Following intravenous, intrathecal and intratracheal administration, LC-1 achieved up to 79% Cas9-mediated knockout in liver and 48% and 27% in brain and lung, up to fourfold higher than LP-01 and ALC-0315, and produced higher ABE-mediated reporter correction across all three routes. LC-1 supported base editing of PCSK9, CFTRR55X and Ube3a-ATS. Mechanistic studies showed that, unlike the benchmarks, LC-1 forms stronger lipid–RNA interactions and retains an ordered, fusogenic inverted-hexagonal structure and pH-responsive membrane disruption as mRNA size increases, rather than becoming disordered. These findings establish cargo size as a key design parameter for ionizable lipid discovery. Lipid nanoparticles are improved by including RNA cargo size in the design process.
nc04c3b0a6c20: Using data from over 3 million people, researchers trace the ancestral history of the EGFR T790M germline mutation and its present contribution to lung cancer risk in those who never smoked.
n9c58b0149aaf: A technique known as prime assembly expands the capabilities of prime editing, allowing larger genome rearrangements and potentially wider clinical applications.
